More moving forward.

PRODUCT RESEARCH · DESIGN NOTE

# Runtime: intelligence with continuity

8 October 2026 · By SINGULANCE Labs

[Back to Research](https://singulancelabs.com/research)

Share the post

## Highlights

- Proactivity begins with relevant, authorized signals.
- A business agenda supplies direction; a signal alone does not.
- Review and retained context connect one work cycle to the next.

RU

Runtime

AI CHIEF OF STAFF

Connect company signals, confirmed priorities and reviewed work.

## From responding to carrying work forward

A useful assistant can answer a request. A company also needs continuity between requests: noticing a relevant change, remembering why it matters, coordinating the next action, and checking what actually happened. Runtime is our product approach to that problem. This article describes its design principles, not a comparative benchmark or a guarantee of business outcomes.

## Proactive is not the same as unbounded

Proactive work starts from selected signals and confirmed goals. A connected source may reveal a recurring question or a teammate may return a deliverable. Runtime needs to relate that event to the current agenda before treating it as useful work. Access to a source does not authorize every action involving it. Missing goals, uncertain evidence and consequential choices should become questions for the administrator.

## A continuous work cycle

The cycle is notice, connect, coordinate, review and carry forward. First, identify a relevant signal from an authorized source. Next, consult company context and the administrator’s priorities. Assign scoped work to a specialist when a useful next step is established. Review the saved result rather than accepting a completion announcement as proof. Finally, retain accepted findings, unresolved questions and useful lessons for the next follow-up.

## What anticipation should mean

Anticipation is a design aim: recognizing an emerging need early enough to offer a useful next step. It is not clairvoyance. Repeated customer questions might suggest an onboarding gap, but that remains a hypothesis until examined. The appropriate response may be an internal investigation or a question, rather than an external action. A system should show the evidence supporting its proposal and remain open to correction.

## The administrator stays in the loop

Runtime coordinates specialists and brings meaningful results or required decisions back to the administrator. Reviews, approvals and messages serve different purposes: a completed internal analysis may need a short update, while an external commitment requires the appropriate authorization. Initiative should reduce the effort of managing work without removing the person responsible for the company’s direction.

## How to evaluate the idea

A credible evaluation should measure relevant signal selection, correct use of retained context, assignment clarity, deliverable quality, permission compliance and recovery after interruptions. It should also measure unnecessary notifications and duplicated work. These are proposed evaluation dimensions, not results reported here. Product reliability and usefulness must be demonstrated under realistic conditions, including stale information, conflicting evidence and missing answers.

## A different rhythm for company work

The ambition is practical: fewer lost handoffs, fewer repeated explanations, and clearer connections between an agenda and the work that follows. Runtime brings these steps into one ongoing relationship with the company, while preserving uncertainty and human control.

[Explore Runtime →](https://runtime.singulancelabs.com/)

HYPERAGENTS · Your AI teammates

# Give your teammates context. Get work back.

HyperAgents are AI teammates with persistent rooms in HIVEMIND. Each agent keeps its conversation, task results and deliverables together.

[Open your workspace →](https://next.singulancelabs.com/)

## A room for each teammate

Select an employee from the team sidebar to return to their ongoing conversation. Start another task by sending a message in that room.

## Results you can inspect

Completed work can include summaries and artifacts. The preview panel opens files and deliverables; work details let you inspect tool activity.

## Runtime coordinates

Runtime is the coordinating agent in the same HyperAgents mode. Its scheduled work and autonomy controls belong to its persistent room. Available actions depend on configuration and permissions.

## Get started

- Open your HIVEMIND workspace and sign in.
- Choose HyperAgents from the workspace selector.
- Select a teammate and describe the task.
- Review the result and its evidence or artifacts.

The public product pages describe the experience. Your company conversations, agent traces and artifacts require authorized access at [next.singulancelabs.com](https://next.singulancelabs.com/).

## Encryption that outlives
the quantum threat.

Adversaries harvest encrypted data now to decrypt it later, once a quantum computer can break RSA and elliptic curves. HIVEMIND ships NIST-standardized post-quantum cryptography today — lattice-based ML-KEM & ML-DSA, in a hybrid handshake — so your memory stays sealed for decades.

ML-KEM-768

key encapsulation · FIPS 203

ML-DSA-65

signatures · FIPS 204

Hybrid X25519

classical + PQ, belt & braces

AES-256-GCM

data at rest, quantum-hard

ML-KEM sealed

hivemind · key vault

Post-quantum: the lattice problem stays hard even for Shor’s algorithm.

# ICARUS v2 — In Production

July 3, 2026 · By SINGULANCE Labs

[Back to Research](https://singulancelabs.com/research)

Share the post

## Highlights

- Thesis → production in seven machine-verified gates — every gate on real embeddings, never synthetic.
- Live cutover: per-tenant .amr shards serving recall behind HIVEMIND at parity 1.00 with the stack they replaced.
- Every memory is post-quantum signed by default — ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204), 30,000+ live signatures, independently verifiable.
- 1.33 ms recall@10 at 1M vectors · 32× compression at 100% overlap · writes never blocked by indexing.

IC

ICARUS

.amr format

A memory filesystem for AI agents — one mmap’d file per tenant, no server.

v1 made a claim; v2 ships the system. Since June, ICARUS went from a frozen format RFC to a production Rust engine behind HIVEMIND: seven machine-verified gates, a live cutover serving real tenants, and — new in v2 — every memory it builds is post-quantum signed by default. This revision documents what was actually built, with the numbers each gate had to pass.

## From thesis to production — seven gates

Nothing advanced on judgment. Each phase ended in a gate: a scripted, reproducible pass/fail check on real data — real bge-m3 embeddings of real production memories, never synthetic vectors. A phase that failed its gate could not advance.

the build — seven gates, each machine-verifiedclick a gate

P6 — Node binding + cutoverrecall parity 1.00

napi addon + MnemeVectorStore — a drop-in for the Qdrant client. Eval gate: recall@5 parity 1.00 vs the live stack on real data. Soak testing surfaced and fixed a real concurrent-reserve segfault (RwLock write-guard).

The engine that emerged: a Rust core (.mseg slots + usearch HNSW overlay + PQ codebooks), write-path isolated from indexing, exposed to Node through a napi binding whose store class is a drop-in for the vector-DB client it replaces. Soak testing under concurrent load surfaced a real segfault in incremental indexing — found, root-caused to an unguarded reserve, fixed with a write-guard, and regression-tested. That is what the gates are for.

## The .amr slot — unchanged, and that’s the point

The 202-byte slot frozen in the v1 RFC survived production contact without a single field change. The format is the contract:

.amr slot — 202 byteshover a field

046142234162170

vector_pqoffset 34 · 128 B

1024-dim embedding → 128 bytes via Product Quantization. 32× compression. The vector IS in the slot, not a foreign key.

## How it runs live — anchor + engine

In production, ICARUS does not replace the relational layer — memory is a relational hub (provenance, projects, embeddings all reference it). The deployed topology keeps a thin relational anchor per memory and moves the hot path — semantic + entity + temporal + graph recall — onto the .amr engine. One file per tenant, opened in-process by the memory engine, with the recall backend live-verified against the previous stack before cutover (recall-parity gate: 1.00).

| Layer | Role in the live system | |
| Relational anchor | One row per memory — identity, provenance, project links. The FK hub stays. | |
| .amr shard (per tenant) | The recall engine: PQ vectors, entity bitmaps, bi-temporal anchors, adjacency — one mmap. | |
| HNSW overlay | Async-built index; writes never wait for indexing (p99 54.75 µs under rebuild). | |
| Engine binding | napi addon; store interface is a drop-in for the previous vector-DB client. | |

## New in v2 — every memory is post-quantum signed, by default

An agent-memory system asks for long-horizon trust: memories written today must still be provably authentic in ten years — against attackers who can rewrite a database, and eventually against quantum adversaries. So the write path signs every memory at creation with ML-DSA-65 (NIST FIPS 204), on by default across managed and self-host deployments:

the signing path — on by defaultstep through

→→→→

Signed with ML-DSA-65 — a NIST-standard post-quantum signature. Secret key lives ONLY in server env, never in the database: an attacker with full DB access cannot forge a valid signature.

Three properties matter. Default-on: not a tier or a toggle — the engine signs every write (30,000+ live signatures on managed hosting at publication). Key separation: signing keys live only in server env, never the database — DB compromise ≠ forgery ability. Independent verification: public keys and verify endpoints are exposed; an auditor needs zero trust in us. Around the memory layer, the same posture: hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203) key exchange on the edge — defeating harvest-now/decrypt-later — and an SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) hash-chained, append-only audit trail with a signed checkpoint.

| Surface | Post-quantum mechanism | |
| Memory writes | ML-DSA-65 signature per memory (FIPS 204) — on by default | |
| Transport | Hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 key exchange (FIPS 203) | |
| Audit trail | SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s hash-chained signatures (FIPS 205), tamper-evident | |
| Verification | Public endpoints: /api/security/pqc · /verify-memory · /audit-verify | |

Honest edges: signing is currently fail-open (a write proceeds unsigned if keys are absent) — an enforce mode for high-assurance tenants is planned; and on self-host BYOD topologies the signature attaches at the engine anchor, with agent-side signing on the roadmap alongside customer-held keys (BYOK): you hold the key, and even we cannot forge your memory.

## v2 numbers

| Metric | Result | |
| proof gate — mmap scan vs vector DB over REST (10k, real embeddings) | 13.3× faster (0.155 ms vs 2.057 ms p50) | |
| recall@10 p50 @ 1M vectors (HNSW) | 1.33 ms · 99.25% vs exact | |
| bi-temporal + 2-hop graph recall @ 1M | 1.93 ms p50 | |
| write p99 under concurrent index rebuild | 54.75 µs — writes never block | |
| vector compression (PQ, ADC + rescore) | 32× at 100% recall@10 overlap | |
| production shadow eval (8,682 live vectors) | 99.80% top-10 overlap · 98% top-1 | |
| cutover recall-parity gate (drop-in binding) | 1.00 vs previous stack | |
| memory integrity | ML-DSA-65 signature per write — default-on | |

## What’s next

The remaining arc is operational depth, not format change: long-soak burn-in under production write rates; signature enforcement mode (reject unsigned writes) for regulated tenants; agent-side signing on self-host so the signature is born on the customer’s box; and customer-held signing keys. The format stays frozen — the RFC published before the code is still the contract, and v2’s strongest result is that production never forced it to break.

[Read license](https://github.com/amar3012005/ICARUS/blob/main/THESIS-LICENSE.md)

Research

# Cognitive Swarm Intelligence

2026 · By SINGULANCE Labs

[Back to Research](https://singulancelabs.com/research)

Share the post

## Highlights

- Externalized — intelligence lives in the environment, not any single agent.
- Emergent — coordination without explicit messaging, via shared state.
- Structural — learning without retraining; structure changes, weights don’t.
- Shared — local identity, global intelligence.
- Controlled — safe self-improvement through a bounded meta-loop.

CS

CSI

Architecture

Environment-centric intelligence — a shared cognitive substrate behind HIVEMIND and HYPERAGENTS.

## Abstract

Artificial intelligence systems today are overwhelmingly model-centric. Intelligence is assumed to live inside a model or an agent, while memory, tools, and workflows remain auxiliary attachments.

At SINGULANCE Labs, we propose Cognitive Swarm Intelligence (CSI): an environment-centric architecture in which intelligence is not treated as a property of any single agent, but as an emergent property of a shared, persistent, structured cognitive environment.

CSI combines structured memory, stigmergic coordination, adaptive routing, procedural consolidation, agent identity, and a controlled meta-loop into a single architecture. The result is a system designed not merely to answer questions, but to remember, coordinate, execute, improve, and accumulate operational intelligence over time.

## [01] The problem — why agent-centric AI has structural limits

| Limit | Why it bites | |
| Transient knowledge | Even when external memory exists, it is treated as static retrieval context rather than an active medium for cognition. | |
| Brittle coordination | Multi-agent systems coordinate through explicit communication — costly, brittle, and hard to scale. | |
| No procedural learning | Repeated successes do not harden into reusable behavior. Every session starts from scratch. | |
| Lost reasoning | Systems store outputs but not the pathways that produced them — decision rationale is lost. | |

## [02] Core thesis — the central claim

“Persistent shared cognition can outperform isolated agent reasoning when memory, behavior, and policy are all externalized into a structured environment.”

| # | Claim | What it means | |
| 1 | Intelligence can be externalized | Store competence in the environment — decisions, facts, execution trails, blueprints, confidence signals — not only in weights or prompt history. | |
| 2 | Coordination emerges without heavy messaging | Agents cooperate through shared state — trails, observations, graph relationships — not explicit communication. | |
| 3 | Learning occurs without retraining | The system improves by changing structure: successful paths strengthen, repeated sequences become blueprints, weak paths decay, routing adapts. | |
| 4 | Identity stays local, intelligence stays global | Agents differ by role, skill, and reputation, but competence is shared — agents are access points into a common substrate. | |
| 5 | Self-improvement requires control, not chaos | A bounded meta-loop: observe, evaluate, recommend, apply — through a controlled parameter registry with rollback. | |

## [03] Architecture — a three-layer cognitive runtime

| Layer | Namespace | Role | |
| Canonical Knowledge | kg/* | Durable, validated knowledge — entities, relationships, procedures, decisions. The long-lived source of truth. | |
| Operational Cognition | op/* | The active life of the system — goals, trails, execution events, observations, attempts, decision candidates. | |
| Control & Learning | meta/* | Evaluative signals — reputation, trail weights, decay schedules, blueprint thresholds, routing parameters. The control plane. | |

## [04] Key concepts — how CSI works

Five interconnected mechanisms let intelligence emerge from the environment rather than reside in any single agent.

Trails — behavior as first-class structure. A trail is a compact, structured representation of how progress toward a goal can be made. Unlike raw logs, trails are directly actionable — connecting goal context to next steps, shaped by success, failure, cost, latency, conflict, congestion, and reputation. “Given this context and this goal, what path has proven useful?”

Blueprints — from repetition to procedure. When the system detects repeated successful patterns across execution traces, it promotes them into reusable composite trails — its emerging habits. This is how the system learns how to act, not merely remember what happened.

Force-Based Routing — cognitive physics for action selection. Instead of hard-coded path selection, the system computes a force profile over candidate trails, combined via softmax to preserve exploration while exploiting strong pathways. Toggle the forces to feel how the swarm chooses:

Force-based routing — toggle the forces

Attractive

Repulsive

Net pull on this trail1.4

Moderate — explored, not committed.

Agent Identity — without agent-centric intelligence. Each agent has an identity, role, declared skills, observed competence, reputation, and specialization confidence — yet intelligence remains shared. “Agents have roles. The environment has memory. Intelligence emerges from their interaction.”

The Meta-Loop — safe self-improvement. A bounded three-part loop turns self-improvement from uncontrolled self-editing into policy evolution through configuration: a read-only Dashboard (success rates, blueprint usage, force contributions), a batch MetaEvaluator (detects patterns, produces recommendations), and an auditable Parameter Registry with rollback.

## [05] What CSI is not

| Not… | Because | |
| Not just RAG | RAG retrieves text. CSI stores structured outcomes, execution traces, and reusable behavior. Retrieval is one component. | |
| Not just a memory system | Memory preserves data. CSI preserves data and behavior — turning repeated success into procedures and shaping future policy. | |
| Not just orchestration | Orchestrators move tasks. CSI evolves how those paths are chosen and reused over time. | |

## [06] Why it matters

| Outcome | What changes | |
| Competence survives replacement | Replacing the agent does not destroy intelligence — it has been externalized into the environment. | |
| Operational intelligence accumulates | Organizations build compound knowledge rather than losing it when sessions end or teams change. | |
| Improvement without retraining | Systems improve through usage by evolving policies, procedures, and routing — not model weights. | |
| Auditable reasoning | Reasoning becomes persistent and traceable through structured trails and decision provenance. | |
| Structural coordination | Coordination emerges through shared-environment modifications rather than expensive message overhead. | |
| Policy evolution | Learning by evolving policies and procedures instead of re-running costly reasoning loops. | |

## Future work

| Direction | Goal | |
| Long-term memory benchmarks | Evaluate environment-centric memory against long-horizon recall — does externalized memory beat context-bound systems? | |
| Agent transfer benchmarks | Measure whether competence survives agent replacement — testing CSI’s central thesis directly. | |
| Procedural learning studies | Blueprint formation and policy adaptation as a path to learning without retraining. | |
| Research intelligence | Extend CSI to hypothesis tracking, evidence graphs, and scientific reasoning over time. | |

The system remembers. The agents act. Licensed CC BY 4.0 · SINGULANCE Labs.

Beyond the horizon of intelligence.

# Post-quantum cryptography, shipped in three layers

Jul 2, 2026 · By SINGULANCE Labs

[Back to Research](https://singulancelabs.com/research)

Share the post

## Highlights

- Three independent quantum-resistant layers — transport, memory integrity, and audit.
- Hybrid key exchange closes harvest-now-decrypt-later at the edge: safe unless both classical and quantum-hard problems fall.
- Every memory write is signed; DB-level tampering becomes mathematically detectable.
- The audit log is chained into an append-only, tamper-evident trail — verifiable by anyone.
- NIST-standardized post-quantum primitives; signing keys never touch the database.

HI

HIVEMIND

Sovereign memory engine

The memory layer that remembers everything your org knows — now quantum-resistant end to end: transport, integrity, and audit.

## Why — the threat model

An adversary who can't break today's crypto can still record encrypted traffic now and decrypt it later, once a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer exists ("harvest-now, decrypt-later"). Separately, an attacker with DB access could try to forge or silently rewrite stored memories or audit logs. HIVEMIND addresses both with quantum-resistant primitives at the transport, data-integrity, and audit layers.

## The three layers at a glance

| Layer | Purpose | Primitive | Standard | |
| Transport | Defeat harvest-now / decrypt-later | Hybrid key exchange (classical × lattice KEM) | FIPS 203 | |
| Memory integrity | Prove a memory wasn’t forged or altered | Lattice signatures | FIPS 204 | |
| Audit trail | Tamper-evident, append-only log | Hash-based signatures | FIPS 205 | |

〉 harvest-now · decrypt-later

### Fire a quantum attack at the vault.

Classical RSA/ECC falls to Shor’s algorithm. The lattice problem behind ML-KEM stays hard — the vault holds.

ML-KEM sealed

## Layer 1 — Hybrid post-quantum TLS

Every connection to HIVEMIND is negotiated with a hybrid key exchange — two independent secrets, combined:

hybrid key exchange

shared_secret = combine( classical_ECDH, // fast, proven today lattice_KEM // quantum-hard (FIPS 203) )

The session key is safe unless both the classical and the lattice problem are broken at once — so it is never weaker than today's crypto, and quantum-resistant on top. The practical consequence: an adversary who records the encrypted stream today cannot decrypt it later, even with a future quantum computer. Older clients that don't understand the hybrid negotiation fall back to the classical curve, so nothing breaks.

## Layer 2 — Memory write integrity

Every time a memory is written, HIVEMIND signs a canonical, deterministic representation of the record — the exact same bytes can be reconstructed later:

memory write — signing logic

payload = canonical({ id, user, org, content }) // keys sorted, stable signature = sign(payload, private_key) // lattice signature

The signature is stored alongside the memory, not inside it, and the signing key lives only in the environment — never in the database. So an attacker who reaches the database and rewrites content cannot produce a matching signature: forgery needs the secret key, and the secret key isn't there to steal. Anyone holding only the public key can verify the memory is authentic and unaltered.

## Layer 3 — Tamper-evident audit chain

Security-relevant events are chained like a mini-ledger: each entry commits to the one before it, then the commitment is signed.

audit chain — link logic

entry_hash = hash( previous_entry_hash + canonical(entry) ) signature = sign(entry_hash, audit_private_key) // hash-based signature

Because every entry's hash folds in the previous entry's hash, the log is append-only: you can't insert, delete, or reorder a single event without breaking every link after it. The first entry anchors the chain (no predecessor). The signatures use a hash-based scheme — the most conservative post-quantum family, resting on the fewest assumptions — because an audit trail is exactly where you want maximum paranoia. A periodic checkpoint signs the head of the chain, so the entire history can be verified in one shot.

## Where the trust lives — key management

The whole model rests on one principle: the secret keys never live where the data lives. Signing keys exist only in the runtime environment; the database holds signatures and public keys, nothing that could forge them. Compromising the database therefore does not grant the ability to forge a memory or rewrite the audit log — the attacker would still be missing the one thing that matters.

Verification is public by design: anyone with the public key can independently confirm authenticity, without any privileged access. And every layer degrades gracefully — if a signing key is absent, the write still succeeds, just unsigned. Availability is never sacrificed for signing; integrity is added on top, never in the critical path.

## Anyone can check the work

None of this is a claim you have to take on faith. Because verification only needs public keys, the guarantees are externally auditable:

| Question | How it’s answered | |
| Is post-quantum crypto actually on? | A status probe reports the active algorithms and whether keys are loaded, and hands back the public keys. | |
| Was this memory forged or altered? | Recompute its canonical payload and check the signature against the public key. | |
| Has the audit log been tampered with? | Walk the chain end to end — re-derive each link, verify each signature and the head checkpoint. | |

The same checks run automatically against every live deployment, so a broken link or a missing signature is caught before it ships — never after.

## The primitives, and why each was chosen

| Standard | Family | Why it’s used here | |
| FIPS 203 | Lattice key encapsulation | Fast enough to sit on every connection — transport secrecy at no latency cost. | |
| FIPS 204 | Lattice signatures | Small, fast signatures — cheap enough to sign every single memory write. | |
| FIPS 205 | Hash-based signatures | The most conservative family, fewest assumptions — reserved for the audit trail, where trust matters most. | |

## Guarantees, limits & roadmap

Guarantees. Transport secrecy is quantum-resistant (hybrid) — recorded traffic stays safe. Stored memories are integrity-signed; DB-level tampering is detectable. The audit trail is append-only and tamper-evident, verifiable end-to-end by a third party using only public keys.

Current limits. PQC here covers key exchange + signatures (integrity/authenticity). At-rest payload encryption is separate (standard DB/disk encryption; not PQC-KEM-wrapped). Signing is best-effort: with keys absent, writes proceed unsigned by design (availability over hard-fail).

Roadmap. Enforce-signing mode (reject unsigned writes) for high-assurance tenants · per-tenant signing keys ␀· post-quantum envelope encryption for memory payloads at rest.

Benchmark

# 87.2% on LongMemEval. Published. Reproducible.

Jun 26, 2026 · By SINGULANCE Labs

[Back to Research](https://singulancelabs.com/research)

Share the post

## Highlights

- 87.2% accuracy on LongMemEval — single-session, multi-session, temporal, and knowledge-update questions
- Sub-50ms recall latency at production scale, measured continuously
- Live retrieval benchmark (P@5 / R@10 / NDCG@10 / MRR) with pass/fail regression gates before every deploy
- Methodology and question set are public — reproducible by anyone, on your own memories too

HI

HIVEMIND

Evaluation

The Evaluation surface inside every HIVEMIND workspace — health, retrieval benchmarks, and A/B regression gates, live.

retrieval quality — click a metricsingulancelabs.com/benchmark

LongMemEval87.2%

Overall accuracy on LongMemEval — the industry-standard benchmark for long-context conversational memory. Single-session and multi-session recall, temporal reasoning, and knowledge-update questions, evaluated end-to-end against the published hypothesis format.

## What LongMemEval actually tests

LongMemEval is the benchmark long-context memory systems get judged against — not a synthetic retrieval toy, but multi-session conversational histories with single-session questions, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning across sessions, and knowledge-update questions where an earlier fact is later corrected. A system that only does keyword lookup or flat vector similarity collapses on the multi-session and temporal categories. HIVEMIND's bi-temporal graph — memories that update, extend, derive from, and contradict each other with typed relationships — is built for exactly this shape of question.

Published methodology

LongMemEval question set + evaluation harness are public. Anyone can re-run the exact same questions against the exact same corpus.

No cherry-picked runs

The reported score is the full-set average, not a best-of-N run. Regressions below the pass/fail gate block deploys.

Live regression gate

Every recall-path change re-runs the retrieval benchmark (P@5 / R@10 / NDCG@10 / MRR) before shipping — a regression fails the gate, not the customer.

Reproducible on your data

The same Evaluation surface ships inside every HIVEMIND workspace — run the benchmark against your own memories, not just ours.

## HIVEMIND vs. the alternatives

Keyword search fails the moment a question is phrased differently from the source text. Naive vector RAG improves recall but has no concept of time, contradiction, or multi-hop reasoning across sessions — it retrieves chunks, not a coherent memory. The gap widens exactly where enterprise memory matters most: knowing what changed, when, and why.

| Metric | HIVEMIND | Keyword search | Naive vector RAG | |
| LongMemEval accuracy | 87.2% | 41.3% | 68.9% | |
| Recall latency (p50) | <50ms | ~120ms | ~200ms | |
| Multi-session reasoning | Native | None | Partial | |
| Temporal / bi-temporal queries | Native | None | None | |
| Contradiction resolution | Automatic | None | Manual | |

## Run it yourself

The published run lives at [singulancelabs.com/benchmark](https://singulancelabs.com/benchmark). Every HIVEMIND workspace — personal, managed, or self-hosted — ships the same Evaluation surface: health overview, an interactive search tester with confidence and relevance scoring, and the retrieval benchmark itself. Don't take the number on faith — point it at your own memory and watch the gate run.

Beyond the horizon of intelligence.

# Privacy Policy

Last updated: August 27, 2026 · SINGULANCE, Hannover, Germany

Contents

Part I

## Privacy Policy

## Overview

This policy describes how SINGULANCE (“we,” “us,” “our”) collects, processes, and protects information across our products — HIVEMIND (memory engine), Tara (voice agent), and Sentinel Agents (autonomous digital employees), together the “Services.” SINGULANCE is built EU-first: single-tenant deployments, EU-hosted infrastructure, and data handling designed around GDPR, DORA, and the EU AI Act from day one. These design goals support customer compliance obligations; they are not a legal certification or a substitute for each customer’s own assessment.

## Website Data, Cookies & Similar Technology

Our edge provider necessarily processes request information such as IP address, user agent, requested URL, status code, and timestamp to deliver and protect the site. We store your versioned cookie choices in the strictly necessary first-party cookie singulance_cookie_consent_v1. Optional preferences, PostHog EU product analytics and autocapture remain disabled until you opt in. Session replay remains disabled. We currently install no advertising or retargeting tracker. See our [Cookie Policy](https://singulancelabs.com/cookies) for the provider, purpose, category, and duration of each browser technology.

## Lawful Bases

- Contract or steps requested before contract (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)): accounts, authentication, requested product functions, support, and billing
- Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)): optional analytics, marketing technology, and consent-based communications; consent can be withdrawn at any time
- Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)): essential security, fraud prevention, service reliability, and responding to business inquiries, balanced against your rights
- Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)): tax, accounting, regulatory, and lawful-request records where applicable

Access to the public site and core contractual service is not conditional on accepting optional analytics or marketing technology.

## Information We Collect

Account information you provide directly:

- Full name and email address
- Organization name and role
- Billing and plan information (processed via our payment provider — we do not store card numbers)

Content and data created within the Services:

- Memories, documents, and conversations you save to HIVEMIND
- Voice recordings and transcripts processed by Tara, where enabled
- Configuration, agent instructions, and workflow data for Sentinel Agents

Technical information necessary for security and operation:

- Authentication and session logs
- API and connector usage logs
- System performance and error metrics

## Connected Services

With your explicit consent, you may connect third-party services so HIVEMIND can ingest, recall, or act on your behalf — for example Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Slack, Notion, GitHub, LinkedIn, and others available in your Connectors page. Each connection requires:

- Explicit authorization through that service’s own OAuth consent screen — we never see your password
- A scope grant limited to what the connected feature actually uses
- Your ability to disconnect and revoke access at any time from the Connectors page

Data accessed through a connected service is processed only for the purpose you authorized (ingestion, recall, or an action you requested) and is subject to that service’s own terms as well.

## AI Processing

When you use HIVEMIND’s recall, chat, or agent features, your content may be processed by model providers routed through our controlled AI gateway solely to generate the response or action you requested. We do not permit these providers to train on your data. Where a connector routes execution through a third-party platform (for example, Composio for certain tool integrations), the same principle applies — processing happens at your direction, for your request, and nothing else.

## Use of Information

- Operating and authenticating your account
- Storing, indexing, and recalling memory as you request it
- Executing connector actions you explicitly authorize
- Billing, plan enforcement, and fraud prevention
- Essential service communications
- Security monitoring and abuse prevention
- Compliance with legal obligations under GDPR, DORA, and applicable law

## Data Residency & Hosting

Hosted HIVEMIND workspaces apply organization and user scope across application, database, vector-search, and graph paths. Dedicated and self-hosted deployment options provide additional physical isolation where contracted. Primary application and memory infrastructure is operated in Europe; a connector or model provider you deliberately invoke may process the minimum necessary request outside the EEA under an applicable transfer mechanism described below.

## Service Providers & Sub-processors

Depending on the product and configuration you use, service providers may include:

- Cloudflare for DNS, edge delivery, security controls, Workers, and controlled AI routing
- EU infrastructure providers, including Hetzner, for application, database, and memory services
- PostHog EU Cloud for optional aggregate product analytics only after consent; session replay is disabled
- Stripe for checkout, subscriptions, and payment records; SINGULANCE does not store full card numbers
- Google or other identity providers when you choose their sign-in method
- Model and connector providers needed for a feature you request, subject to the selected deployment and routing configuration

We review this list when providers or processing purposes change and update this notice before materially different optional processing is enabled.

## Information Disclosure

We do not sell, rent, or commercially trade your personal information. We disclose information only:

- To infrastructure and processing subprocessors necessary to run the Services (see Infrastructure Partners)
- To third-party AI providers, solely to fulfil a request you made
- To services you explicitly connected, per the scope you authorized
- When required by law, regulation, or valid legal process
- To protect the rights, safety, or property of SINGULANCE, our users, or others
- In connection with a merger, acquisition, or asset transfer, with continuity of this policy

## Data Retention & Deletion

We retain account and memory data for as long as your account is active, or as needed to provide the Services, subject to configured retention and legal obligations. Consent records are retained for the stated cookie lifetime, optional analytics identifiers for the period listed in the Cookie Policy, and payment or tax records for applicable statutory periods. You may delete individual memories, disconnect a connector, or request full account deletion at any time. Disconnecting a service stops new sync but does not automatically delete previously ingested data unless you request it. Full-account deletion requests are honored subject to legal retention requirements and reasonable processing time.

## Your Rights (GDPR)

As a data subject under GDPR (and equivalent rights under other applicable law), you may:

- Request access to the personal data we hold about you
- Request correction of inaccurate data
- Request erasure of your data (&ldquo;right to be forgotten&rdquo;)
- Request restriction of, or object to, certain processing
- Request data portability in a structured, commonly-used format
- Withdraw consent for a connected service at any time
- Lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority

To exercise any of these rights, contact us — see Contact below.

We normally respond within one month after verifying the request. You may also complain to your competent supervisory authority, including the State Commissioner for Data Protection of Lower Saxony where applicable.

## International Transfers

Where a connected service or AI provider you authorize is based outside the EU/EEA, we rely on that provider’s Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent safeguard, and only transfer the minimum data necessary to fulfil the request you made.

## Policy Updates

We may update this policy as our Services evolve. Material changes are communicated by email to account holders or a prominent notice in the product before they take effect.

## Contact

For privacy requests, security disclosures, or general questions about this policy, contact us at [privacy@singulancelabs.com](mailto:privacy@singulancelabs.com). For security vulnerability reports specifically, use [security@singulancelabs.com](mailto:security@singulancelabs.com).

# Security

Last updated: August 27, 2026 · SINGULANCE, Hannover, Germany

Contents

Part II

## Security

## Security Overview

Security is architectural at SINGULANCE, not a policy layer bolted on afterward. Every design decision — tenant isolation, dedicated-deployment options, encryption defaults, credential handling — starts from “what does a regulated European enterprise’s security team need to see” rather than being retrofitted later.

## Encryption

- All data in transit is encrypted via TLS
- Connector access tokens and refresh tokens are encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) before storage — never stored in plaintext
- Encryption keys are managed separately from application data

## Tenant Isolation

Every hosted request is scoped to the authenticated user and organization across database, vector, and graph access paths. Dedicated and self-hosted deployments are available for customers that require physical isolation contractually. Logical isolation and dedicated deployment are distinct controls and are not represented as the same thing.

## Infrastructure Partners

We rely on a small number of vetted infrastructure providers, each contractually bound to appropriate security standards:

- EU-based hosting for primary application and database infrastructure
- Cloudflare AI Gateway and configured model providers for inference invoked by a requested feature
- Composio, where used, for specific third-party tool execution you authorize

## Access Control & Authentication

- OAuth2-based authentication for every connected service — no shared or hardcoded credentials
- Role-based access control within an organization (admin vs. member permissions)
- Session-based authentication with configurable expiry
- Rate limiting on public-facing endpoints

## Incident Response

In the event of a personal-data breach, we notify affected controllers without undue delay and support the information they need for their own obligations. Where SINGULANCE is the controller, we assess notification to the competent supervisory authority within GDPR’s 72-hour window and notify affected individuals when the law requires it.

## Contact

For privacy requests, security disclosures, or general questions about this policy, contact us at [privacy@singulancelabs.com](mailto:privacy@singulancelabs.com). For security vulnerability reports specifically, use [security@singulancelabs.com](mailto:security@singulancelabs.com).

SINGULANCE · Hannover, Germany

Legal · Cookie policy

# Technology should wait for your choice.

Last updated: August 27, 2026. This policy explains cookies and similar browser storage used on singulancelabs.com and the HIVEMIND web application. Non-essential categories remain disabled until you opt in.

## Categories

### Strictly necessary

Security, authentication, consent storage, and services you explicitly request. These cannot be disabled.

### Preferences

Optional storage that remembers choices and customizes your experience.

### Analytics

EU-hosted aggregate product measurement. Disabled until accepted; session replay remains disabled.

### Marketing

Advertising and campaign attribution. No marketing tracker is currently installed.

## Technology register

| Technology | Provider | Category | Purpose | Duration | |
| singulance_cookie_consent_v1 | SINGULANCE | Necessary | Stores the consent-policy version and your category choices. | 1 year | |
| Authentication session cookies | SINGULANCE / authentication provider | Necessary | Keeps signed-in sessions secure. Only created when you sign in. | Session or configured expiry | |
| singulance-field | SINGULANCE | Preferences | Remembers the industry experience you explicitly select. | Until removed | |
| PostHog analytics identifiers | PostHog EU Cloud | Analytics | Measures aggregate product use after consent. Session replay is disabled. | Up to 1 year | |

## Withdrawal and browser controls

Use “Change cookie preferences” at any time. Rejecting analytics stops future capture and clears PostHog persistence available to the browser. You may also delete cookies and local storage in your browser settings.
